newsitem.title: USA: WTO's Ruggerio hopeful of telecom, ITA pacts.
newsitem.headline: WTO's Ruggerio hopeful of telecom, ITA pacts.

text.p: The head of the World Trade Organization said Monday he was hopeful that agreements could be struck in the next few months on removing trade barriers in telecommunications and information technology.
WTO director general Renato Ruggiero cited both sectors during a speech sponsored by the Institute for International Economics, a think tank.

"We have not succeeded completely. But we have arrived very close to a conclusion. With a strong will, we can arrive at a conclusion on schedule in (February) 1997," Ruggiero said, referring to telecommunications talks.
Ruggiero said he wanted to consult Acting Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky about last weekend's "Quad" meeting of trade officials from Japan, Canada, the European Union and the United States.
During the meeting, U.S. and EU officials agreed to sweeten their offers in hopes a global agreement could be reached to open telecommunications markets.
U.S. and EU officials also opened the way for renewed negotiations on a global Information Technology Agreement.
Ruggiero expressed hope of agreement soon on information technology at the same time he mentioned telecommunications.
The ITA would eliminate duties on a number of electronic products, including computers, software, computer chips and telecommunications equipment by 2000.

Ruggiero said he hoped the December meeting of trade ministers in Singapore, the first meeting since creation of WTO, would result in "a strong political message on a rules-based system" for trade between nations.
